title: Unified column resize affordance and multi-filter gestures for high‑cardinality tables
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background:
We maintain multiple table variants across the product: highly dense admin logs, wide attribute grids, and compact search results. Engineering has reported increased complexity when trying to reconcile column resizing affordances with the virtualized rendering layer and keyboard accessibility. Current problems: invisible resize hit targets on narrow rows, conflicts between hover-only handles and touch/trackpad gestures, and inconsistent auto-fit behaviors when data is streamed in or when the KV cache/virtualization reorders rows.

Goals:
- Define a single, discoverable column-resize affordance that works across desktop (mouse/trackpad), touch, and keyboard;
- Harmonize auto-fit/double-click behavior for text and numeric columns so widths are stable under virtualization;
- Introduce a compact density variant that preserves usable resize handles;
- Surface clear sorting/filtering affordances that don’t collide with resize gestures;
- Minimize runtime complexity for ENG: avoid adding per-cell listeners and keep DOM changes minimal to preserve virtualization performance.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Resize interaction failure rate <= 1% on instrumented sessions (via console telemetry);
- Time to resize a column (first successful drag) median < 350ms on desktop;
- Keyboard-only users can resize and reset to auto-fit (verify with ARIA tests and WCAG checks);
- No regressive perf impact measured in runtime e2e perf tests (batching/vdom renders).

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Hover-only handles are elegant on desktop but inaccessible on touch; adding always-visible handles increases visual noise. We propose a hybrid: compact visible gripper for all densities that collapses to a 6px hit area but expands on hover/focus.
- Double-tap/double-click to auto-fit is expected by power users, but double-tap on mobile conflicts with text selection and column reordering gestures. We'll scope double-tap to pointerType=mouse and provide a contextual menu action on touch.
- Avoid attaching resize listeners to each header cell. We'll use event delegation at the header row container and calculate target column by data-attribute, preserving virtualization-friendly DOM.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Visual affordance:
   - Always-render a subtle 6px gripper at the right edge of each column header. The gripper expands to a 14px visible handle on hover/focus. For compact density, the expanded visual is slimmer but still accessible.
   - Use token-driven spacing and hit sizes (tokens: spacing-xxs, hit-area-md) so changes propagate via the design system.

2) Interaction model:
   - Pointer (mouse/trackpad): drag to resize; double-click to auto-fit (only for mouse); press Alt/Option + drag to proportionally resize adjacent columns.
   - Touch: long-press to reveal a larger handle and show contextual menu with "Resize to fit" and preset widths (S/M/L).
   - Keyboard: header cell receives focus via Tab/Shift+Tab; when focused press Enter to open a mini-resizer overlay that supports ArrowLeft/Right to nudge by token units and Home to auto-fit. Escape to close.

3) Sorting/filtering coexistence:
   - Sort affordance remains on the left half of the header; filter (funnel) is on the right interior, inset from the gripper. We add a 4px radial padding between filter and gripper hit targets and add visual separators on hover to reduce accidental mis-taps.

4) Virtualization and auto-fit stability:
   - Auto-fit computes column width using the sampled visible rows plus a headless cell-measure cache per column (bounded to first 200 rows). When virtualization evicts rows, the cache remains until a write-invalidation is triggered (e.g., new model load or explicit dataset change). This reduces width jitter as virtualization swaps DOM nodes.
   - Implementation requirement for ENG: expose a small API to invalidate column-measure caches when model/series changes.

Design deliverables:
- Figma exploration file: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/Table-Resize-UX (variants: desktop / touch / compact)
- Interaction spec doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Table+Resize+Interaction+Spec
- Annotated handoff tokens: tokens/table.json (token names included in spec)

Open questions for review:
- Should double-click auto-fit be allowed for trackpad taps that emulate mouse clicks on macOS? (proposal: allow when pointerType===mouse or when event.detail>1 and not on iOS)
- For large tables with many columns, should we introduce a column-width lock toggle to prevent accidental wide resizes?

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (design + prototype): deliver Figma + HTML prototype (no virtualization) - complete by 2026-01-31.
- Phase 2 (ENG integration): ENG implements delegated handlers + measure cache (ENG-2941). Iterative testing with telemetry flags.
- Phase 3 (opt-in): behind a console flag for 10% of customers, monitor telemetry and accessibility outcomes.

Notes to ENG/PM:
- Engineering asked to avoid per-cell listeners; the proposed approach uses data-col-id attributes and a delegated pointer handler.
- Performance tests should include large table rendering with 100k rows virtualized; ensure that our handle expand-on-hover purely affects pseudo-element styling where possible to avoid layout thrash.

Known risks:
- Touch long-press discoverability may be low; mitigate by adding a short tooltip/coach for first-time users inside the console.
- Auto-fit metric relying on sample cache could mismatch if visible rows are not representative; we'll add a periodic re-measure when the user actively resizes neighboring columns.

Acceptance criteria:
- Figma approved by design lead; interaction spec reviewed by ENG and PM; prototype validated in accessibility tests; ENG implements event-delegation and measure cache with a PR and unit tests; telemetry shows no regression in average render time on main table page.
comments: 2026-01-20 - Kickoff: met with ENG (Oliver, Priya) and PM (Diego). Agreement on delegated handler approach. ENG flagged need for a small cache invalidation API.

2026-01-28 - Prototype ready: HTML prototype uploaded to Figma prototype link. Usability microtest with 5 designers: compact gripper visible but not noisy — lukewarm feedback on long-press discoverability.
2026-02-02 - ENG feedback: suggested making auto-fit calculations incremental to avoid blocking main thread. We'll add a web-worker-friendly sketch for measure caching.
2026-02-18 - Design review: clarified keyboard overlay interactions and ARIA roles. Added explicit guidance for screen reader announcements when column width changes.
2026-03-03 - PM review: requested telemetry events for 'resize_started', 'resize_committed', 'auto_fit_triggered' with column id and pointer type. Added to spec.
2026-03-09 - Accessibility review: recommended increasing expanded handle to 18px on focus, confirmed that visual change is token-driven.
2026-03-10 - Pre-handoff: final spec updated with token names and sample CSS variables. Ready for ENG handoff (see attachments).
